notes: Zone core_grounds: what stands in or on the lawns of the core area and no other model has. Written by /tmp/claude-0/p5/core/core_grounds/gen.py; the JSON is the source now and may be edited by hand. Frame: model metres, +X east, +Y grid north, Z NAVD88. Red Hawk Catholic (OSM 232850502, the Newman centre, 894 Valley Road; not in the published model): four parts fitted in a frame along its walls (-23.9 degrees, the east roof edge is straight to 0.3 m at that angle in the 2017 LiDAR), each edge at the outermost roof return, so the walls may stand up to 0.3 m inside the eaves. Ground round it 114.9 to 115.6 m. Main block hip, ridge 126.7, eaves 122.3 (the real roof is cross-gabled); a one-storey wing on the south (shed, 119.1 to 123.0), a one-storey wing on the north (dark roof, gable across it, 119.0 to 121.6) and a low bay on the west (119.8). The ground in the south-west corner of the house is a terrace at ground level (no returns over 1 m). Paving: the entrance apron east of the house (level with it, 115 m), a walk 1.3 m wide from the end of the steps (core_ways' cw_walk_232850506 ends in it) round the south and east walls to the apron, a lower court 2.3 m down east of the apron (111.5 to 112 m, white L-shaped walls in the ortho, drawn on the raw ground), and the walk from it towards Valley Road as far as the outline (OSM 232850574; core_ways does not draw this footway). East of the yard the LiDAR ground drops 2.1 to 2.3 m within a metre to the Valley Road verge (109.5 m), and the court has a 2.3 m wall on its west side: these retaining walls are not drawn, because a wall stands on the paved grade (terrain.at), which next to the apron reads the apron's 115 m, so they would float 3 to 5 m over the low side; the soft ground takes the drops as steep banks. No drive or parking of its own shows inside the outline: the dark paving south of the house belongs to the house next door, outside. Science Quad ponds: OSM's two intermittent ponds (2018) lie 4 to 10 m off what the ortho and LiDAR show; the ponds are the two grey-green lobed basins of the 2020 ortho (91.8 and 65.1 m2 traced; OSM 66 and 75 m2), 0.4 to 0.6 m under the lawn in the 2017 LiDAR (north basin ground 136.83, 136.91, 137.16 m at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles; south 136.98, 137.03, 137.16). Both are dry in both sources. Each is drawn as a gravel shore on the basin and water 0.6 m inside it (north 77.3 and 47.6 m2, south 39.6 and 19.2 m2 inside the outline: their east parts run under the main model's CELS eaves and stay out). Beds (mulch): the planting west of the north pond (OSM garden 552441195) and the planted triangle between three walks (OSM garden 552441013), traced by hand on a 1 m grid on the 7.5 cm ortho; the planting west of the south pond is not in OSM and stays lawn. Low walls (OSM, missing from the published model): the arc by the amphitheatre (287541788, a circle fitted to the white coping, rms 0.11 m), and two in the Student Center Quad (313024785, 313024786): their long runs moved onto the step fitted across them in the LiDAR ground (0.15 to 0.3 m off OSM, rms 0.11 m), short runs on OSM; brick by the reddish coping in the ortho. Along 313024785 core_ways' brick plaza (cw_brick_plaza_313024784) runs 1.2 to 1.8 m past this step onto the lower lawn, so the wall stands on its paving. OSM walls 313024771 and 313024772 (by University Promenade, x -101..-109, y 152..177) are not drawn: the 2017 LiDAR shows no step and no returns over 0.2 m on them. Bike racks: the five OSM bicycle_parking nodes (2026) inside the outline, rows set along the nearest walk; the published model has racks only at the College of Communication and Media. Benches: none drawn; the ortho cannot tell a bench from a planter at 0.15 m and OSM maps none here. The wooded slope east of Life Hall and the College of Communication and Media stays base lawn; its trees come from tools/evidence/trees.py. Fix-up pass (edited by hand): cg_red_hawk_walk follows the raw ground (grade false): its graded west end stood 1 m over the LiDAR at the foot of the steps.
